Consonantal i

Theme

Playground equipment, sandbox toys, vehicles and play

bait noun

also bait the hook

classical

Traupman 46

1ēsca: long e (Lewis & Short leaves it unmarked). De Vaan (s.v. edō) derives it from *ed-sk-ā; the same cluster gives the long e of ēst, “eats”, and ēsus. The series spells it so.

ēsca1, ēscae f.

noun, first declension

The series spelling. For hāmus, hook, see the hook entry.

Examples

  • ēscam hāmō impōnere

    put the bait on the hookTraupman 47

  • Ēscam hāmō impōne et exspectā.

    Put the bait on the hook and wait.composed

See also fishing rod, fish, hook.

SourcesLewis & Short: esca

John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency (printed page numbers): pp. 46–47.

The example sentences marked “composed” are ours.
